'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

1. `authority` is active **and derived**: an authority with no origin is rejected.
2. It is held by the current frame, or by a place `p` on which the current frame has exercisable `Modify`.
3. No active descendant of the authority prevents its release; no other still-usable value may lose a required anchor.
4. If the authority is stored in its holding place, that place is exempted from the check “this authority still appears among the anchors” **only because the effect removes that anchor at the same time**. An anchor with the same identity attached by `depend` to another usable place continues to block the step.
5. Applicable abstraction contracts remain satisfied.

**`ok` effect:** The authority becomes inactive and can no longer be exercised. It is removed from its holding place's anchors when stored there. Effective modes of its origins are recomputed, allowing unblocked rights to return. There is no implicit deallocation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

# IX. Transfer, Dependencies, and Storage of Rights

These transitions govern value consumption and the controlled movement of their dependencies. A valid transition can neither create an additional permission nor discard a surviving anchor.

## 63. O4 — Consuming Value Transfer

**Preconditions**

1. `source` and `destination` are usable, and the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over their relevant footprints.
2. Source and destination have the **same shape of ordered subtrees**. The `i`-th child of each source part corresponds to the `i`-th child of the corresponding destination part; all nodes are matched. Structural field identity is positional, not an arbitrary matching of children.
3. **All** source leaves are `Init`, and **no** destination leaf is `Init`. The source and destination footprints are disjoint.
4. No exclusive authority is duplicated; validity of derived authorities and active projections is preserved. No active derived authority held outside `source` covers a source leaf, except the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right over `source`: the exercisable authority on which that right rests and its origin chain. Other active authorities remain subject to this check. Authorities held by parts of `source` are transferred with the value and are controlled by §63.8.
5. **No in-place source leaf is pinned**, either statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (`pin`). Storage merely **owned** by the source, which is not itself moved by the transfer of that value, does not prevent this transfer.
6. Dependencies of all still-usable places following the value remain valid; non-escape constraints and `AnchorOrder` are checked in the **resulting state**, including transferred anchors of owned places that remain usable.
7. All moved held authorities, including those of owned storage, satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` in the resulting state; no authority may escape a local anchor on the grounds that its containing value was transferred.
8. **Local self-blocking prevention:** For each active authority held before the step by a part `r` of `source` whose holder becomes the corresponding part `corr(r)` of `destination`, that authority's footprint contains **no leaf** of `corr(r)` in the resulting state. Transfer is rejected if this local check fails; no global authority-acyclicity check is imposed.
9. **Destination usability:** `destination` is usable in the resulting state.

**`ok` effect:**

- every source leaf becomes `Moved` and each corresponding destination leaf becomes `Init`;
- every authority held by source part `r` acquires as its new holder the corresponding destination part `corr(r)`, not indiscriminately the destination root;
- places owned by `r` become owned by `corr(r)`; their roots follow this owner according to `RootHeld`;
- value dependencies follow the corresponding places under validity guarantees; no authority is created or duplicated;
- destination places receive the transferred values and rights without automatically moving storage not owned by a source part.

**Other outcome:** `reject`. `transfer` to a call result is subject to these same rules.

A partially initialized structure may be transferred **field by field**, but only for fields individually eligible for transfer. This does not automatically destructure a value that owns storage **at the container level**: that storage stays with the container if the container is not transferred. Conversion between structures with permuted fields must be handled separately, not as a `transfer`.

## 64. O5 — Explicit Attachment of an Anchor

**Preconditions**

1. `result` is a usable place over which the current frame has exercisable `Modify`.
2. `anchor` designates an active, valid authority representing a real dependency of the relevant rights or storage; a declared dependency cannot extend an origin's lifetime.
3. Existing anchors are preserved and the addition respects `AnchorOrder`: the effective anchor's frame is the frame of `result` or an ancestor thereof.
4. Every dependency carried by a contained value remains represented in the transitive obligations of its container.

# ERN — Memory Model Specification v0.1

**Edition v0.1 — corrective candidate, not yet validated**

Modified clauses, relative to v0 (each change is justified by a defect found while formalizing v0):

- §36: `MetaRight` governs authorities over existing storage, not the fresh allocation of `alloc`; §36 and §71.2 contradicted each other.
- §40: `RootHeld` restricted to usable root places, as in §49.7; the two clauses differed on unusable root places.
- §47: the ownership graph of statics is acyclic; a static ownership cycle made §57 false in the initial state.
- §51: a valid origin is an active origin; "valid" was undefined there.
- §57: definition of I5, which v0 named without defining.
- §59: "access operations" are O9–O11; read as all operations, §59 contradicted §69.
- §60.1: a valid origin chain is an active one, read through §44.
- §63.4: the active derived authorities covering the source from outside are named, and the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right are exempt; without this exemption no value could be moved through a derived authority.
- §63.9 (new): the destination is usable in the resulting state; without it an accepted transfer could create an ownership cycle and break §49.8 and §57.
- §69.2 and §70.3: the same exemption as §63.4, and rejection when an authority made inactive by the step keeps an active descendant; without it an accepted step left an active authority with an inactive origin.
- §71.2: the provider is a usable place; v0 did not require it to exist.
- §74 and §75: each `pin` installs an obligation of fresh identity and `unpin` ends one designated obligation; per-leaf pin flags let an `unpin` lift a pin installed by another `pin`.
- §76.6: the reading of the precondition (whole kernel state, `ArenaInv` of the new entry, resulting state); v0 admitted several readings with different verdicts.
- §78.3: restricted to anchors covering a leaf of the administered storage; as written, its second sentence was false.
- §82.2: address and provenance of a pointer to a region whose leaves all have zero physical size; v0 decided no address for that region.
- §86: the last sentence is rewritten; as written, it was false, since `reset` and `issue` leave a recycled leaf `Init` and readable.

**Higher normative authority:** *ERN — Language Charter v0* (October 27, 2026).  
This specification defines the normative rules of ERN's memory model. Technical names (`derive`, `transfer`, `issue`, etc.) designate **abstract semantic operations**; they do not constitute syntax decisions.

## Validation and Revision Procedure

This edition is a corrective candidate, not yet validated; it acquires normative authority under the ERN Charter v0 only once validated. Any subsequent semantic change must identify the clauses concerned, justify the change, and preserve the guarantees of the ERN Charter v0. Formal models and proofs are instruments for verifying this specification, not sources of additional rules. Behaviors not determined within its scope are explicitly identified.

# ERN — Memory Model Specification v0.1

**Edition v0.1 — corrective candidate, not yet validated**

Modified clauses, relative to v0 (each change is justified by a defect found while formalizing v0):

- §36: `MetaRight` governs authorities over existing storage, not the fresh allocation of `alloc`; §36 and §71.2 contradicted each other.
- §40: `RootHeld` restricted to usable root places, as in §49.7; the two clauses differed on unusable root places.

makes the block authority 5, held by the value 2, inactive while its derived authority 8 (origin 5)

/-! ## `I1`–`I4`, `NoDangling`, `Inv3` (§50–§54, §57) -/

/-- `I1` (§50): two distinct active authorities unrelated by derivation covering a common leaf
both have own mode `Observe`. -/
def I1 (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (a b : Nat) (x y : Authority) (p : Nat), a ≠ b → s.A[a]? = some x → s.A[b]? = some y →
    x.active = true → y.active = true → p ∈ x.footprint → p ∈ y.footprint →
    a ∉ s.ancs b → b ∉ s.ancs a → x.mode = .observe ∧ y.mode = .observe

/-- `I2` (§51): the origin of a derived authority exists; the derived mode does not exceed the
origin's, the derived footprint is within the origin's, and the origin of an active derived
authority is valid, that is, active. -/
def I2 (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (b : Nat) (y : Authority) (a : Nat), s.A[b]? = some y → y.origin = some a →
    ∃ x : Authority, s.A[a]? = some x ∧ y.mode.le x.mode ∧ (∀ p ∈ y.footprint, p ∈ x.footprint) ∧
      (y.active = true → x.active = true)

/-- `I3` (§52): every anchor of a usable place is valid (active). -/
def I3 (s : S3) : Prop := ∀ q, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, s.Active x

/-- `I4` (§53, first sentence): no read of a region containing a `Moved` leaf is permitted. -/
def I4 (s : S3) : Prop := ∀ (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat) (l : Nat), l ∈ ls → s.I l = .moved →
  ¬ Read3Pre s a ls

/-- `writeShared` as a relation (§68). -/
def WriteSharedStep (k : K) (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (WriteSharedPre k s a ls) (write3Eff s ls)

/-! ## Release of authorities whose holder dies (§69, §70) -/

/-- Releases every authority whose holder is no longer live (§69, §70 `ok` effects). -/
def cleanup (s : S3) : S3 :=
  { s with A := s.A.map fun y => if HolderLive s y.holder then y else { y with active := false } }

/-! ## O12 `endUse` (§69) -/

/-- `endUse p` before releasing authorities whose holder died (§69, `ok` effect): the leaves of
`p` become `Uninit`; authorities held within `p` are released; anchors of `p` and its parts are
removed; storage owned by `p`, transitively, is marked dead. -/
def endUseS (s : S3) (p : Nat) : S3 :=
  { s with
    I := fun l => if l ∈ footprint s.P p then .uninit else s.I l
    D := fun q => if partOf s.P q p then [] else s.D q
    dead := fun q => s.dead q || decide (OwnedIn s.P p q)
    A := s.A.map fun y => if heldIn s.P p y.holder then { y with active := false } else y }

/-- Effect of `endUse p` (§69, `ok` effect): `endUseS`, then the authorities whose holder died
are released. -/
def endUseEff (s : S3) (p : Nat) : S3 := cleanup (endUseS s p)

/-- Leaf whose use ends with the value at `p` (§69.2, §69.4): a leaf of `p` or of storage that
stops being usable. -/
def EndingLeaf (s : S3) (p l : Nat) : Prop :=
  l ∈ footprint s.P p ∨ (isLeaf s.P l ∧ s.Usable l ∧ ¬ (endUseS s p).Usable l)

/-- Decidability of `EndingLeaf` (§69). -/
instance (s : S3) (p l : Nat) : Decidable (EndingLeaf s p l) := by
  unfold EndingLeaf; infer_instance

/-- Root authority of the value at `p` (§69.3): an authority with no origin covering a leaf of
`p`. -/
def IsRootOf (s : S3) (p : Nat) (y : Authority) : Prop :=
  y.origin = none ∧ ∃ l ∈ footprint s.P p, l ∈ y.footprint

/-- Decidability of `IsRootOf` (§69.3). -/
instance (s : S3) (p : Nat) (y : Authority) : Decidable (IsRootOf s p y) := by
  unfold IsRootOf; infer_instance

/-- Authority `j` does not block `endUse p` (§69.2): if it is an active derived authority over an
ending leaf, it is held within `p` or its holder dies. -/
def EndUseAccessOK (s : S3) (p j : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun y => y.active = true → y.origin ≠ none →
    (∃ l ∈ y.footprint, EndingLeaf s p l) →
      heldIn s.P p y.holder ∨ ¬ HolderLive (endUseS s p) y.holder) True

/-- Decidability of `EndUseAccessOK` (§69.2). -/
instance (s : S3) (p j : Nat) : Decidable (EndUseAccessOK s p j) := by
  unfold EndUseAccessOK OptP; split <;> infer_instance

/-- Anchor `x` survives `endUse p` (§69.3): not held within `p`, not a root of `p`, with a holder
that stays live. -/
def EndUseAnchorOK (s : S3) (p x : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[x]?) (fun y => ¬ heldIn s.P p y.holder ∧ ¬ IsRootOf s p y ∧
    HolderLive (endUseS s p) y.holder) True

/-- Decidability of `EndUseAnchorOK` (§69.3). -/
instance (s : S3) (p x : Nat) : Decidable (EndUseAnchorOK s p x) := by
  unfold EndUseAnchorOK OptP; split <;> infer_instance

/-- Preconditions of `endUse` (§69). -/
structure EndUsePre (k : K) (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- §69.1: `place` is usable. -/
  usable : s.Usable p
  /-- §69.1: exercisable `Modify` over `place`. -/
  right : HasRight s .modify p
  /-- §69.2: no active derived authority over an ending leaf is held outside the dying places,
  except the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right over `place`: some
  authority grounding that right and its origin chain. -/
  access : ∃ g ∈ List.range s.A.length, Grounds s .modify p g ∧
    ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, RightChain s g j ∨ EndUseAccessOK s p j
  /-- §69.2, last sentence: no authority that the effect makes inactive has an active descendant
  that the effect does not make inactive. -/
  keptDesc : ∀ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, s.Active a →
    ¬ (endUseEff s p).Active a → a ∈ s.ancs j → ¬ (endUseEff s p).Active j
  /-- §69.3: no place usable after the effect depends on an authority held by `place`, its root,
  or an authority whose holder dies. -/
  anchors : ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (endUseS s p).Usable q →
    ∀ x ∈ (endUseS s p).D q, EndUseAnchorOK s p x
  /-- §69.4: no ending leaf, owned storage included, is pinned, statically or dynamically. -/
  notPinned : ∀ l ∈ List.range s.P.length, EndingLeaf s p l → s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l

/-- Decidability of the preconditions of `endUse` (§69). -/
instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Decidable (EndUsePre k s p) :=
  decidable_of_iff (s.Usable p ∧ HasRight s .modify p ∧
    (∃ g ∈ List.range s.A.length, Grounds s .modify p g ∧
      ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, RightChain s g j ∨ EndUseAccessOK s p j) ∧
    (∀ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, s.Active a →
      ¬ (endUseEff s p).Active a → a ∈ s.ancs j → ¬ (endUseEff s p).Active j) ∧
    (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (endUseS s p).Usable q →
      ∀ x ∈ (endUseS s p).D q, EndUseAnchorOK s p x) ∧
    (∀ l ∈ List.range s.P.length, EndingLeaf s p l → s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l))
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f⟩, fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f⟩⟩

/-- `endUse` as a relation (§69). -/
def EndUseStep (k : K) (p : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (EndUsePre k s p) (endUseEff s p)

/-! ## O13 `free` (§70) -/

/-- The holder is a place (§70.1). -/
def Holder.isPlace : Holder → Bool
  | .place _ => true
  | .frame _ => false

/-- `OwnedRoot` (§70.1): a place with no structural parent, owned by a place. -/
def OwnedRoot (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.P[p]?) (fun pl => pl.parent = none ∧ pl.owner.isPlace = true) False

/-- Decidability of `OwnedRoot` (§70.1). -/
instance (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Decidable (OwnedRoot s p) := by
  unfold OwnedRoot; infer_instance

/-- Place `q` belongs to the unit released by `free p` (§70): a part of `p`, or storage owned by
`p`, transitively. -/
def FreedPlace (P : List Place) (p q : Nat) : Prop := partOf P q p ∨ OwnedIn P p q

/-- Decidability of `FreedPlace` (§70). -/
instance (P : List Place) (p q : Nat) : Decidable (FreedPlace P p q) := by
  unfold FreedPlace; infer_instance

## 51. I2 — Conservation of Rights

A derived authority covers only a subfootprint of what its origin chain permits and does not elevate its mode. Derivation and splitting restrictions do not allow duplication of an exclusive right over a leaf. Every active authority is linked to a valid origin according to state and reanchoring rules: an origin is **valid** if and only if it is active, so the origin of an active derived authority is active. Partial suspension follows from `effective`.

## 52. I3 — Validity of Anchors and Dependencies

Every explicit anchor of a still-usable place is valid. An operation cannot invalidate an anchor retained by a place that remains usable. Transitive propagation of dependencies from contained values does not change this obligation. Dependencies are not permissions and are insufficient to justify an access.
----
## 69. O12 — Logical End of a Value's Use

**Preconditions**

1. `place` is usable and the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over it.
2. No active descendant over the leaves of `place` **or storage that dies with it** is held outside the places dying with `place`, in a way that would prevent rights from returning or being invalidated. The authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right over `place`, namely the exercisable authority on which that right rests and its origin chain, are exempt from this check. Moreover, no authority that the effect makes inactive (held by `place` or by a place dying with it, transitively owned storage included) has an active descendant, whatever its footprint, that the same step does not make inactive.
3. No place **remaining usable after the effect** depends on an authority held by `place`, its root, or an authority that would become inactive when an owned holder dies.
4. **No leaf whose use ends, including transitively owned storage, is pinned**, either statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (`pin`). A dynamic pinning obligation must be legally removed by `unpin` before this step.

**`ok` effect:** The leaves of value `place` become `Uninit`; `place` **remains usable as a place** and may legally be reinitialized. Authorities held by `place` and dead substorages are released; dependencies of the ended value are removed; transitively owned places that cease to live are marked dead. The operation does not automatically trigger physical deallocation in the elementary memory machine: an unfreed allocation may constitute a leak, which this guarantee does not prohibit. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 70. O13 — Release of an Owned Storage Unit

- HP5-7 (Q4): every library step is, on the kernel side, a sequence of accepted kernel steps O1–O16; the

      else if l ∈ footprint s.P src then .moved else s.I l

/-- Active derived authority covering a leaf of `src` and not held within it (§63.4). -/
def ActiveDerivedOutside (s : S3) (src j : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ y.origin ≠ none ∧ ¬ heldIn s.P src y.holder ∧
    ∃ l ∈ y.footprint, l ∈ footprint s.P src) False

/-- Decidability of `ActiveDerivedOutside` (§63.4). -/
instance (s : S3) (src j : Nat) : Decidable (ActiveDerivedOutside s src j) := by
  unfold ActiveDerivedOutside; infer_instance

/-- The holder moves with the value at `src` (§63.6, §63.7): a part of `src` or storage it owns,
transitively. -/
def HolderMoves (s : S3) (src : Nat) : Holder → Prop
  | .place p => partOf s.P p src ∨ OwnedIn s.P src p
  | .frame _ => False

**Verdict: ok.** The two spec edits and the H49 change do what the decisions ask and nothing more. No finding blocks this. One low finding, plus a note on the PR's state.

**Spec edits**

`git diff specs/` changes exactly two lines. No other normative clause changed, and the list of modified clauses in the header was left as it was.

- **Line 29.** "This edition has been validated and acquires normative authority…" now reads "This edition is a corrective candidate, not yet validated; it acquires normative authority under the ERN Charter v0 only once validated." This matches line 3 ("corrective candidate, not yet validated"). The added "only once validated" agrees with the Charter (`specs/ERN_Language_charter_v0.md:187`, "Validated specifications constitute the normative reference"). The rest of the section is unchanged.
